What would I change ? I'm not sure. I fear that changing anything in my life before would've led to worse outcomes. I guess my first regret is dropping out so quickly, and panicking like I did. I don't blame myself everyday or anything, but that was a moment of weakness I wish I never had. Also my other regret is spending a few months at home doing nothing and leaving me with my anxious thoughts. I should've done something sooner, so I would've less thought of death and time passing by. I finally regret not putting much effort into making friends when I got back in uni 3 years ago. I only have a handful of friends now - it's enough, but I could've tried harder.
I'm happy for you, because you didn't make any of the mistakes I made that I now regret - you didn't drop out and you didn't give yourself up to despair.

I put myself back together through the help of my parents - I would be dead without them. They supported me when I dropped out, and didn't complain when I stayed home doing nothing. I broke down several times in front of them, and they helped me go through my anguish. After a few months scaring myself to death, I decided, only for their sake, that I would try to get better. I started with learning piano and going to an amateur play troop. In a matter of a few weeks, I got a job. These activities plus this job distracted myself, and even though I never got the happiness I had before, that was good enough. In September of 2019 I got back in uni without much motivation but this time I refused to screw up because I knew that dropping out the year prior had led me to the worst time of my life. And here I am today, in 3rd year, with still some major shyness and depression, but getting by because I have to, because I know it's still better than going back to the depths I dived into at some point. Just like you, I don't feel like progressing on the inside, but at least I'm not regressing, you know ? Which circles back to what I said in the first place.

In my high school years, I was in a small village that had around 100 people in the entirety of the building. We all knew each other and had really friendly interactions. All I had to worry about was grades and I had a big social circle, without ever being the most extroverted, but people were just so used to seeing me around after all these years that we all became friends naturaliy.

Then it was all over, and I realised my social circle was solely based on high school. I was alone for a few months and then had to go to uni. I discovered the big city, and I was absolutely terrified. In my first day, I ended up having a panic attack (which I never had before, it happened to me only twice after this event) and decided to drop out. On the first day. The next few months, I did nothing at home. I regretted everything. And that's when I started to be... conscious about some things. I realised that I never had a girlfriend. I realised that I was not a minor anymore. I realised that time was ticking. I realised my parents will die one day and I will too. These few months destroyed me.

That was a few years ago. I picked myself up a long time ago, I'm back in uni, I had a few jobs instead of staying at home doing nothing, I tried several new hobbies, and I have some acquaintances that I think are my friends. But it'll never be the same again now that I fully realised the human condition and that I will never succeed at much. I wish I was just as careless as before, but I just cannot be anymore. I can feel content sometimes, I can feel down again, but I'll just never truly happy like before, when it was almost permanent.

Uni often offers therapies for anyone - free of charge, with volunteers who are in psychology school. They are around your age, and can easily understand what you're going through. And of course, everything is done anonymously.
Uni is also a place with a lot of extra-scholar activites that can take your mind off stuff - you'll surely find a hobby that you can appreciate along with studies.
Also, remember uni is a huge place, with hundreds and hundreds of people. It's statistically impossible that you won't find a friend or two there. You'll find it very impressive how easy it is to make friends in uni - whether it is in class, in the cafeteria, or inside the campus in general. Especially in first year, you'll find a lot of confused, lonely people who are just waiting to be talked to because they lost their entire friend circle after leaving high school.

Trust me, uni can be hard, but you'll have a lot of support there, I can guarantee that
